English language requirements for postgraduate students
Do I need to provide an English language test score?
Whether you will need to provide an English language test score to evidence your English language ability depends on your educational background.
Decisions are normally taken based on the criteria below, but the University of St Andrews reserves the right to ask for additional evidence of English language ability, for example, an ECCTIS Qualification and Language Service (QLS) English Proficiency and Qualification Comparison verification confirming that the qualification is equivalent to CEFR Level C1, or a language test.
You should not need to provide an English language test score to evidence your English language ability if you meet one of the criteria listed below. However, please note that the University reserves the right to request additional evidence of English language ability, such as a valid English language test score, in relation to any application to the University.
Open all
UK degrees taught in English
You have completed a UK undergraduate degree with at least the final two years taught in the UK, or you have completed a UK postgraduate degree that was taught entirely in the UK.
Degrees from countries where English has official status
You have completed a qualification equivalent to a UK undergraduate or postgraduate degree taught entirely in English at a nationally accredited English-medium university (with provision of verified evidence by the awarding institution that you were taught in the medium of English) in one of the following countries or territories designated by UKVI as being a majority English-speaking country:

Australia

Additionally, we will accept qualifications equivalent to a UK undergraduate or postgraduate degree taught entirely in English at a nationally accredited English-medium university (with provision of verified evidence by the awarding institution that you were taught in the medium of English) from:
Hong Kong
Singapore
South Africa
If you have completed a qualification equivalent to a UK undergraduate or postgraduate degree taught entirely in English at a nationally accredited English-medium university (with provision of verified evidence by the awarding institution that you were taught in the medium of English) in one of the following countries or territories, you will need to provide a verified ECCTIS Qualification Language Service (QLS) English Proficiency and Qualification Comparison Unique Person Identifier (UPI) number and download of your ECCTIS QLS result, confirming the level of English language required for this qualification is equivalent to CEFR Level C1 (statements indicating that a degree programme meets the requirements of CEFR Level B1 or B2 are not acceptable) to satisfy our requirements:

Please note that the University reserves the right to request additional evidence of English language ability, such as a valid English language test score, in relation to any application to the University.
Degrees taught in English and obtained in other countries
Undergraduate or postgraduate degrees which are taught through the medium of English from countries which are not listed in the degrees from countries where English has official status section may also be considered as evidence where the following conditions are met:
The awarding institution features in the top 300 of current QS University Rankings and verified evidence from the awarding institution is provided confirming that the specific applicant has completed a degree that has been taught in English; OR
An ECCTIS Qualification Language Service (QLS) English Proficiency and Qualification Comparison Unique Person Identifier (UPI) number and download of your ECCTIS QLS result is provided confirming the level of English language required for this qualification is equivalent to CEFR Level C1 (statements indicating that a degree programme meets the requirements of CEFR Level B1 or B2 are not acceptable) and verified evidence from the awarding institution is provided confirming that the specific applicant has completed a degree that has been taught in English.
Please note that the University reserves the right to request additional evidence of English language ability, such as a valid English language test score, in relation to any application to the University.
Obtaining an ECCTIS Qualification Language Service (QLS) English Proficiency and Qualification Comparison
If you have studied a degree in a country from a non-majority English-speaking country, you can apply for an English Proficiency and Qualification Comparison from the ECCTIS Qualification Language Service (QLS) confirming that the degree was taught in English to a particular standard. This service can be used where you have completed your degree (it cannot be used if you are still studying for your degree).
In order for the University to accept an ECCTIS QLS verification as evidence of English language, ECCTIS must confirm that the qualification is equivalent to CEFR Level C1. Statements indicating that a degree programme meets the requirements of CEFR level B1 or B2 are not acceptable.
Please note that the University reserves the right to request additional evidence of English language ability, such as a valid English language test score, in relation to any application to the University.
Students who cannot provide any of the evidence mentioned in the three sections above will need to submit a valid English language test score as stated in the programme entry requirements.
Which English language test score should I provide?
This will depend on whether you are a postgraduate taught student or a postgraduate research student.
Postgraduate Taught students
The table below indicates a language profile for each postgraduate subject area. Clicking on a profile link will take you to the list of acceptable tests and scores that you may submit to meet English language requirements for your intended degree.
Test scores are only normally accepted if obtained within two years of the programme start date.
Typically, profiles listed here will include a score on the University’s own ten-week and four-week Academic English Pre-sessional courses, which can be taken to meet English language requirements. See more details on the University of St Andrews Academic English Pre-sessional courses webpage.

Postgraduate Research students
The minimum requirements for any postgraduate research student are detailed in Profile 7-D. Schools will normally require the same English language test scores as those stated for their postgraduate taught programmes, however, individual Schools reserve the right to request higher test scores than this. Current exceptions are:
School of Geography and Sustainable Development: the language requirements for postgraduate research programmes in the School of Geography and Sustainable Development are Profile 6-D (Direct entry).
Typically, English language requirement profiles listed for postgraduate taught students include a score on the University’s own pre-sessional courses. Where included at the discretion of the School, these courses may also be taken to meet English language requirements for postgraduate research students. See more details on the University of St Andrews Academic English Pre-sessional courses webpage.
